# Mātaṅgajātaka (Ja 497)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mātaṅgajātaka* (Ja 497) is a canonical Jātaka belonging to the class of early "ascetic poetry," in which the spiritual self-control and piety of a wandering ascetic are contrasted with the rigid ceremonialism of brahmans [Norman 1983]. According to the frame narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha related this story while residing at Jetavana with reference to King Udena and the Venerable Piṇḍolabhāradvāja, who was accustomed to spending the heat of the day in King Udena's park at Kosambī [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1887]. The birth story (*atītavatthu*) recounts the deeds of the Bodhisatta as the outcaste sage Mātaṅga-paṇḍita and features the figure of Maṇḍavya, who is revealed at the conclusion of the story to have been a former rebirth of King Udena [Fausböll 1887]. The *Dhammapada* commentary also connects one of its narratives to the story of Jātimanta and the Bodhisatta in this Jātaka [Burlingame 1921].
Scholars have highlighted the antiquity of the *Mātaṅgajātaka* due to its close parallels in canonical Jain literature, which share a common heritage of ascetic narrative poetry; while the mutual resemblances are profound enough to demonstrate descent from a common ancestor, both Buddhist and Jain redactors introduced distinctive sectarian adaptations [Norman 1983; Wyyzilic and Stender 2010]. SuttaCentral records thematic or resembling parallels in the *Saṁyutta Nikāya*, specifically the *Jaṭāsutta* (SN 1.23, SN 7.6) and the *Satthāravandanāsutta* (SN 11.19) [SuttaCentral]. According to DharmaNexus matches, passages of the text are shared internally within the Pali tradition with its commentary (*Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, book 4), the *Majjhimanikāya* commentary (*Majjhimapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*), and the anthological *Suttantanīti*, alongside an automatic alignment with the Tibetan *Subhāṣitaratnakaraṇḍakakathā* (D 4168) [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): SN 1.23 Jaṭāsutta; SN 11.19 Satthāravandanāsutta; SN 7.6 Jaṭāsutta
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Catuttho bhāgo) (Atk S0513a4) (§14.4–19.4 ↔ §3875–3889); Majjhimanikāye Majjhimapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0202a) (§1.1–3.4 ↔ §231–244); Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Suttantanīti (Anya E1006n) (§9.1–11.4 ↔ §258–265)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): ལེགས་པར་བཤད་པ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཟ་མ་ཏོག་ལྟ་བུའི་གཏམ། (subhāṣitaratnakaraṇḍakakathā) (D4168) [bo]
